Guerrero joined the insurgent army led by José María Morelos in 1810, quickly demonstrating military aptitude. He played a vital role in battles like Zitltala and Tixtla, where his knowledge of the local terrain and ability to communicate with indigenous people proved invaluable. After Morelos’s death in 1815, Guerrero continued the fight, employing guerrilla tactics and becoming a symbol of resistance, remaining the last major rebel leader at large. He secured victories in various regions of southern Mexico, including Ajuchitán and Santa Fe. 

A turning point came in 1820 when Agustín de Iturbide, initially sent to suppress Guerrero’s forces, ultimately allied with him. This alliance, formalized under the Plan de Iguala, proclaimed Mexico’s independence, established a constitutional monarchy, and maintained the Catholic Church's position. Crucially, Guerrero insisted on including a clause guaranteeing equal rights to all inhabitants regardless of race, dismantling the existing casta system. The Army of the Three Guarantees marched into Mexico City in 1821, marking the end of the war.

Following a period of political turmoil and Iturbide’s brief reign as emperor, Guerrero became president in 1829 amidst contested circumstances. His election was secured through a rebellion led by Santa Anna and the resignation of the elected president, Gómez Pedraza. As a liberal, Guerrero championed reforms, most notably the abolition of slavery throughout Mexico in September 1829, though he later exempted Texas due to pressure from American settlers. He also advocated for public education, land reform, and economic development. 

However, Guerrero’s presidency was short-lived. He was overthrown in a rebellion led by his own vice president, Anastasio Bustamante, bringing an end to his time in office and ultimately leading to his death in 1831. Despite the brevity of his term, Guerrero’s legacy remains significant as a champion of independence, equality, and a popular hero representing the hopes of a truly inclusive Mexico.

title: Danny Faure
text:
Danny Faure, born on May 8, 1962, is a Seychellois politician who served as the fourth President of Seychelles from October 16, 2016, to October 26, 2020. Prior to his presidency, he held the position of Vice-President of Seychelles from 2010 to 2016, and is a member of the United Seychelles Party, formerly known as the People’s Party. 

Faure was born in Kilembe, Uganda, to Seychellois parents, and received his primary and secondary education in the Seychelles itself. He then pursued higher education at the University of Havana in Cuba, where he earned a degree in political science.

His career in public service began in 1985, at the age of 23, when he joined the Seychelles education ministry as an assistant curriculum officer. He also shared his knowledge as a lecturer at both the National Youth Service and the Seychelles Polytechnic. Following the return of multiparty democracy to the Seychelles in 1993, Faure became the leader of government business in the National Assembly, a role he fulfilled until 1998. He subsequently entered the cabinet as Minister of Education. 

Over the years, Faure held a diverse portfolio of ministerial positions, including those relating to youth, finance, trade and industries, public administration, and information and communication technology. A significant period was spent as Minister of Finance, beginning in 2006, where he oversaw economic reforms recommended by the International Monetary Fund from 2008 to 2013. He also served as designated minister from 2004 to 2010, concurrently holding the finance portfolio when he became Vice-President in July 2010.

Faure ascended to the presidency following the unexpected resignation of President James Michel on September 27, 2016, officially taking office on October 16th. This transition occurred alongside an election resulting in an opposition majority in the National Assembly. As Michel’s term had four years remaining, this period counted towards a full presidential term for Faure. During his presidency, he notably drew attention to environmental concerns, delivering a speech from underwater while visiting a British research submersible in April 2019, advocating for stronger ocean protections. This commitment was further recognized in June 2019 when he received the National Geographic Society’s ‘Planetary and Leadership Award’ in Washington D.C.

In the 2020 presidential election, Faure was defeated by Wavel Ramkalawan, marking the end of his time as President of Seychelles. He is a father to five children: four daughters and one son. He married Shermin Rudie Bastienne on April 4, 2021.

title: Ayman al-Zawahiri
text:
Ayman al-Zawahiri, born in Giza, Egypt in 1951 and dying in 2022, was a physician and pan-Islamist militant who became the second emir of al-Qaeda following the death of Osama bin Laden in 2011. He was a key figure in orchestrating the September 11th attacks and was wanted by both the United States and the United Nations for his involvement in numerous terrorist acts, including the 1998 US embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania, and the 2002 Bali bombings. He was killed in a CIA drone strike in Afghanistan in July 2022.

Al-Zawahiri came from a highly educated and politically active family. His father was a surgeon and professor of pharmacy, and his mother was the daughter of a prominent scholar and diplomat who served as the first rector of King Saud University. His family had ties to both religious and political institutions, and even a connection to the Saudi royal family. He excelled in his studies, earning degrees in medicine and surgery from Cairo University. 

He became involved in Islamist activism during his youth, influenced by figures like Sayyid Qutb, and formed an underground cell dedicated to overthrowing the Egyptian government. This led to his involvement with the Egyptian Islamic Jihad, where he rose to the position of emir and was imprisoned from 1981 to 1984 for his role in the assassination of President Anwar Sadat. Even after his release, he continued planning attacks against the Egyptian government, including the 1995 embassy bombing in Pakistan, resulting in a death sentence *in absentia*.

Al-Zawahiri’s path intertwined with Osama bin Laden's in the late 1980s, and their relationship became central to the growth of al-Qaeda. He initially disapproved of some of bin Laden’s operations, such as the 1995 Pakistani embassy attack.  He eventually merged the Egyptian Islamic Jihad with al-Qaeda in 2001 and formally became bin Laden’s deputy in 2004.  He traveled extensively, working as a surgeon in Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, while simultaneously developing and supporting militant networks. 

Throughout the years, his involvement in terrorist activities expanded, extending to attacks in the United States and Pakistan. He was implicated in the USS Cole bombing and the assassination of former Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto. A $25 million bounty was offered for information leading to his capture. He was married multiple times and had several children, some of whom were killed alongside his first wife in a US airstrike in 2001.  Despite years of pursuit, he remained a central figure in al-Qaeda until his death.

title: Ilhan Omar
text:
Ilhan Abdullahi Omar, born in Mogadishu, Somalia in 1982, is currently serving as the U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 5th congressional district since 2019. A member of the Democratic Party, she previously served in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2017 to 2019. She is a prominent figure, being the first Somali American, and the first woman of color to represent Minnesota in Congress, as well as one of the first two Muslim women to serve in the U.S. Congress.

Omar’s early life was marked by the Somali Civil War, leading her family to spend four years in a Kenyan refugee camp before arriving in the U.S. in 1995. The family eventually settled in Minneapolis, where her father worked as a taxi driver and later for the post office. She became a U.S. citizen in 2000.  Her upbringing emphasized the importance of democracy, and she recalls experiencing bullying in school due to her appearance and religious attire. She earned a bachelor's degree in political science and international studies from North Dakota State University in 2011.

Before entering politics, Omar worked as a community nutrition educator and held positions managing campaigns and serving as a policy aide for Minneapolis city council members. In 2016, she was elected to the Minnesota House of Representatives, becoming the first Somali-American legislator in the United States. She then successfully ran for the U.S. House of Representatives in 2018, winning with a significant margin and being sworn in on a copy of the Quran. She has since been re-elected in 2020, 2022, and 2024.

In Congress, Omar is the deputy chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and advocates for policies such as a $15 minimum wage, universal healthcare, student loan debt forgiveness, and the protection of DACA recipients. She also supports abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). She is a vocal critic of Israel, supporting the BDS movement and opposing Israeli settlement policies.  Her views on Israel have attracted controversy and accusations of antisemitism, culminating in a vote by the Republican-controlled House in 2023 to remove her from the Foreign Affairs Committee. 

Omar is a member of "The Squad," a group of progressive female members of Congress advocating for policies like the Green New Deal and Medicare for All. She introduced a resolution supporting the right to boycott as a form of political expression and has introduced articles of impeachment against former President Trump. One of her sponsored bills, designating a Minneapolis post office, became law in 2022.  She has faced scrutiny regarding campaign finance practices, resulting in a requirement to reimburse funds spent on out-of-state travel and a fine, as well as questions regarding joint tax filings.

title: Joey Jordison
text:
Nathan Jonas “Joey” Jordison, born April 26, 1975, and passing away July 26, 2021, was an American musician best known as the original drummer for the heavy metal band Slipknot, identified by the number #1. He was also the guitarist for the horror punk supergroup Murderdolls and involved in numerous other musical projects throughout his career. Jordison grew up in Des Moines, Iowa, beginning to play drums at the age of eight, encouraged by his parents’ preference for radio over television. His parents divorced when he was young, and he took on responsibility within the family, working at his mother’s funeral parlor and playing in bands like Modifidious during his youth.

Before finding fame with Slipknot, Jordison played in a series of bands including The Rejects and Anal Blast, often with future Slipknot members. He joined Paul Gray’s project, the Pale Ones, in 1995, which would evolve into Slipknot. Of the band’s eventual nine-member lineup, Jordison was the third to join. He participated in Slipknot’s first five studio albums and produced their 2005 live album, *9.0: Live*. Alongside Slipknot, Jordison contributed to acts like Rob Zombie, Metallica, Korn, Ministry, and Satyricon, and frequently performed session work for various artists.

In 2002, Jordison revived The Rejects, rebranding them as the Murderdolls, where he played guitar and co-wrote material. The Murderdolls released two studio albums, *Beyond the Valley of the Murderdolls* in 2002 and *Women & Children Last* in 2010, and toured extensively, though their final tour was marred by Jordison’s tinnitus and other issues.  He also founded Scar the Martyr in 2013, which disbanded in 2016, and later formed Vimic and Sinsaenum, the latter being a blackened death metal supergroup he was actively involved with at the time of his death.

Jordison’s departure from Slipknot in December 2013 was initially attributed to personal reasons, but he later revealed he had been fired. He subsequently disclosed a diagnosis of transverse myelitis, a neurological disease that affected his ability to play towards the end of his time with Slipknot. He underwent rehabilitation to regain his physical abilities. 

Throughout his career, Jordison cited influential drummers like Neil Peart, Keith Moon, and John Bonham as inspirations. He utilized various drum brands including Pearl, ddrum, Paiste cymbals, and Promark drumsticks.  Jordison received numerous accolades, including being voted the best drummer of the past 25 years by *Rhythm* magazine in 2010 and being honored with The Golden God Award at the Metal Hammer Golden Gods Awards in 2016. Following his death, numerous musicians paid tribute to his talent and influence. Slipknot dedicated their 2022 album *The End, So Far* to his memory.

title: Diego Suarez (garden designer)
text:
Diego Suarez was born in Bogotá, Colombia in 1888 and died in New York City in 1974. He was a garden designer most recognized for his work on the gardens of James Deering’s Villa Vizcaya in Miami, Florida. His background was steeped in diplomacy and art; his father, Roberto Suarez, was a Colombian diplomat and historian, and his mother, Maria Costa, was Italian. After his father’s death, Suarez and his siblings were raised in Italy. 

He received training in architectural design at the Accademia delle Belle Arti in Florence, where he came under the influence of Arthur Acton. Acton, while restoring the gardens of his Villa La Pietra, imparted Renaissance garden ideals to Suarez, reviving styles favored by designers like Achille Duchêne. Through Acton’s connections, Suarez began designing gardens for wealthy Anglo-Americans in Florence, including projects at Villa Schifanoia for Lewis Einstein and for Charles Loeser, an early collector of Cézanne’s work.

Suarez’s most significant commission came about through a chance encounter. While visiting La Pietra with James Deering and Paul Chalfin, Acton arranged for Suarez to show them various villas. Later, stranded in New York due to the outbreak of war, Suarez reconnected with Deering and Chalfin and was subsequently commissioned to design the gardens at Villa Vizcaya.

The gardens at Vizcaya are designed around the villa’s boat basin, featuring a boat-shaped island, and a south-facing expanse leading to a casino. A key element was a fountain purchased by Deering and Chalfin, which Suarez deliberately placed off the main axis to create a sense of discovery. His design incorporated French baroque-style parterres, contrasts of light and shadow, and subtle changes in elevation to add interest to the flat landscape.

Later in his career, in 1952, Suarez collaborated with architect Frederic Rhinelander King to build a neoclassical house with gardens in Brookville, New York. In 1937, he married Evelyn Marshall Field, the daughter of Charles Henry Marshall and former wife of Marshall Field III, becoming stepfather to Barbara, Bettine, and Marshall Field IV. Diego Suarez is buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in The Bronx, New York City.

title: Ivan Perišić
text:
Ivan Perišić, born in 1989, is a Croatian professional footballer currently playing as a winger for PSV, though he’s versatile enough to play multiple positions including wing-back and attacking midfielder. He is widely considered one of the greatest Croatian players ever. His youth career was spent with Hajduk Split and Sochaux, ultimately signing with Sochaux in 2006 after interest from several other clubs. Though he impressed in the youth ranks, winning the Coupe Gambardella in 2007, he didn't make a first-team appearance for Sochaux, spending time with the B team and a loan spell at Roeselare.

He truly began to make a name for himself at Club Brugge, joining them in 2009. He quickly became a key player, scoring 9 goals in his first season and then topping the Belgian Pro League scoring charts with 22 goals in the 2010–11 season, earning him the Belgian Footballer of the Year award. This success led to a transfer to Borussia Dortmund in 2011, where he won the Bundesliga title. However, his time there was somewhat disrupted by a perceived lack of support from manager Jürgen Klopp, leading to a transfer to VfL Wolfsburg in 2013 for €8 million.

At Wolfsburg, Perišić continued to excel, winning the DFB-Pokal in 2015 and consistently contributing goals. In 2015, he moved to Inter Milan for €16 million, becoming a consistent performer for the club. A loan spell at Bayern Munich in 2019 proved highly successful, as he won the treble – the Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal, and Champions League. Returning to Inter, he added to his trophy cabinet with a Serie A title in 2020–21, the Supercoppa Italiana, and the Coppa Italia in 2021–22.

Perišić has also been a crucial member of the Croatia national team since his debut in 2011, participating in four European Championships (2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024) and three FIFA World Cups (2014, 2018, and 2022). He famously scored an equalizer in the 2018 World Cup final and earned a bronze medal at the 2022 tournament. He is Croatia’s all-time leading goal contributor in major tournaments, with a total of 18 goal involvements, and is seen as a key figure in the nation’s “golden generation.” Throughout his career he has been recognized for his ambidexterity and adaptability, allowing him to thrive in various roles on the field.
